**[1] `mainframe.cpu.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API processor object. In distributed systems terms, a mainframe processor is analogous to a physical CPU core.

**[2] `mainframe.host.machine_model`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API CPC object field `machine-model`. Combined with `mainframe.host.machine_type`, forms the full IBM machine type-model identifier (e.g., "9175-ME1").

**[3] `mainframe.host.machine_type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API CPC object field `machine-type`. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the CPU family or server product line identifier.

**[4] `mainframe.host.serial_number`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API CPC object field `serial-number`. The serial number uniquely identifies a physical mainframe machine.

**[5] `mainframe.partition.name`:** A logical partition (LPAR) is the mainframe equivalent of a virtual machine (VM) in distributed cloud environments. Each LPAR can run an independent operating system such as z/OS, Linux, or z/VM. The name is unique within its Central Processing Complex (CPC) and is the same value every observer reports: the HMC Web Services API partition object field `name`, z/OS RMF (SMF type 70 field `SMF70LPM`) and Linux on IBM Z (`LPAR Name` in `/proc/sysinfo`).

**[6] `mainframe.partition.number`:** Each logical partition on an IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC) is assigned a unique partition number (1–64) by the Processor Resource/Systems Manager (PR/SM). The partition number is static for the lifetime of the LPAR configuration. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to a slot index or NUMA node number — a small integer that identifies a hardware-allocated execution domain. Reported by the HMC Web Services API logical-partition object field `partition-number` (Classic mode). Not applicable in DPM mode where partitions are identified by UUID only.

**[7] `mainframe.partition.type`:** IBM Z Processor Resource/Systems Manager (PR/SM) and Dynamic Partition Manager (DPM) classify each partition by its intended workload type. This controls which processor types the partition may use and which IBM Z software licences apply. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to an instance type or VM profile that constrains what workloads can run on it. Reported by the HMC Web Services API logical-partition or partition object field `partition-type`.

**[8] `mainframe.storage.fulfillment.state`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-group or storage-volume object field `fulfillment-state` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the binding phase of a Kubernetes Persistent Volume Claim.

**[9] `mainframe.storage.group.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-group resource object field `name` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). A storage group aggregates storage volumes of the same connectivity type (FCP, FC, NVMe) that are managed together and can be attached to partitions.

**[10] `mainframe.storage.group.type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-group object field `type` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1).

**[11] `mainframe.storage.group.volume.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API storage-volume resource object field `name` (DPM mode only, HMC ≥ 2.14.1). A storage volume is a single logical unit of block storage (LUN / ECKD DASD cylinder set / NVMe namespace) within a storage group.

**[12] `mainframe.vswitch.name`:** On IBM z/VM, a virtual switch (VSWITCH) is a software-defined Ethernet switch managed by the z/VM Control Program (CP). It connects z/VM guest virtual machines to each other and to physical network adapters (OSA-Express, RoCE). The VSWITCH name is 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters defined in the z/VM CP directory. In IBM Z Dynamic Partition Manager (DPM) mode, virtual switches are exposed as `virtual-switch` objects in the HMC Web Services API. In distributed systems terms, a mainframe virtual switch is analogous to an OVS bridge or a VMware vSwitch. Reported by the HMC Web Services API as the `name` field of the virtual-switch object.

**[13] `mainframe.zvm.guest.userid`:** Each z/VM guest is identified by a unique userid defined in the z/VM CP user directory. The userid is the z/VM equivalent of a virtual machine name on other hypervisor platforms (e.g., a VMware VM name or a KVM domain name). Userids are 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to a virtual machine name or container name. Reported by the HMC Web Services API as the `zvm-guest-name` field on the logical-partition object when the partition is running as a z/VM guest.

**[14] `mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.name`:** The z/VM (z/Virtual Machine) Control Program (CP) runs as a software hypervisor inside a PR/SM logical partition (LPAR). The hypervisor instance is identified by the LPAR name that hosts it. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the hypervisor hostname. Reported by the HMC Web Services API as the `name` field of the logical-partition object that contains the z/VM instance.

`mainframe.cpu.sharing.mode` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | All mainframe processors, both shared and dedicated. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `dedicated` | The processor is dedicated to a specific partition and cannot be shared with other partitions. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `shared` | The processor can be shared among multiple partitions and is not dedicated to a specific partition. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

---

`mainframe.cpu.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aap` | Application Assist Processor (AAP), a processor dedicated to accelerating Java and XML processing for database workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `all` | All types of mainframe processors combined. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cbp` | Container Based Processor (CBP), a processor type for container-based workloads. Present only in HMC/SE versions 2.14.0 through 2.15.0. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cp` | Central Processor (CP), the general-purpose processor that hosts a mainframe operating system such as z/OS. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `icf` | Integrated Coupling Facility (ICF), a processor dedicated to running coupling facility workloads for high-speed communication between systems in a sysplex. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ifl` | Integrated Facility for Linux (IFL), a processor dedicated to running Linux workloads on the mainframe. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `iip` | z Integrated Information Processor (zIIP), a processor dedicated to offloading eligible workloads such as Java applications from general-purpose processors. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `sap` | System Assist Processor (SAP), a processor dedicated to system management and I/O processing workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

`mainframe.partition.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `general_purpose` | General-purpose partition that can run any IBM Z operating system including z/OS, Linux on Z, or z/VM, using all licensed processor types. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `linux_only` | Linux-only partition restricted to running Linux on Z; cannot activate a z/OS or z/VM image. Uses only Integrated Facility for Linux (IFL) processors. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ssc` | Secure Service Container (SSC) partition for IBM Z security appliances; provides a hardware-isolated, tamper-evident execution environment. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | The partition type is not known or could not be determined from the available HMC API response. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `zvm` | Partition configured to host a z/VM hypervisor instance as its primary workload; can manage hundreds of guest virtual machines. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
